chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazid narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever wishes to leave Makkah to perform ʿumrah should enter ihram from al-Jiʿrānah, al-Ḥudaybiyah, or similar places. And whoever leaves Makkah intending ʿumrah and then enters as a muʿtamir should not stop the talbiyah until he looks at the Kaʿbah.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: the ritual invocation recited in ihram
key_terms.الْجِعْرَانَةِ: al-Jiʿrānah, a designated place for entering ihram in this context
key_terms.الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ: al-Ḥudaybiyah, another designated place for entering ihram
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, upon seeing which the talbiyah is not to be cut off before
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the place from which the person departs and re-enters for ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: From where should a person in Makkah enter ihram for ʿumrah, and when should the talbiyah stop?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the miqats for one departing from Makkah to perform ʿumrah, directing such a person to enter ihram from places like al-Jiʿrānah and al-Ḥudaybiyah. It also states that the muʿtamir should continue reciting the talbiyah until seeing the Kaʿbah, clarifying a practical rule of ʿumrah rites.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2952 - Umar ibn Yazid narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Whoever wishes to leave Mecca to perform Umrah should enter Ihram from Al-Ji'ranah, Al-Hudaybiyah, or similar locations. And whoever leaves Mecca intending Umrah and then enters in the state of Ihram should not stop reciting the Talbiyah until they see the Ka'bah."
